stories.title: ‘Very little, if anything, done for KP’: PM Shehbaz rails against PTI’s governance in province
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday criticised PTI’s governance in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, questioning whether the funds available to the now dysfunctional provincial government had been used transparently for the welfare and betterment of the people of the province.

The premier further said that thousands of civilians and security personnel had been martyred during the past two and a half years, adding that the PTI had been offered an opportunity to join hands with the federal government to combat terrorism, as it had done in the past.

The prime minister elaborated that even if the PTI-led KP government had spent Rs80 billion on strengthening the police and other law enforcement agencies, they would have been better equipped to tackle security challenges. “But unfortunately, that did not happen,” he added.

stories.title: Germans join Europe's wave of 'Gen Z' protests; police fire water cannon on demonstrators
summary: In Berlin, Frankfurt, Cologne and dozens of other cities, demonstrators turned out for the protests organised by the group ‘GenZ regelt!’ (GenZ has got this), the latest by disillusioned youth in Europe.

Protesters light dlares after a demonstration organised by “GenZ regelt!” (Gen Z has got this!) in Frankfurt am Mian on October 31, 2026. — AFP Earlier, a march through the city was halted after demonstrators started setting off fireworks.

A policeman stands next to police cars on the sidelines of a demonstration organised by “GenZ regelt!” (Gen Z has got this!) in Berlin on October 31, 2026. — But prior to the protests, authorities said that they had not seen evidence of concrete plans for violence.

stories.title: Pakistan slams Afghan Taliban for 'shifting blame', 'persistent refusal' to address terrorism issues
summary: The information ministry on Saturday rebuked the Afghan Taliban’s stance on the ongoing conflict between the two countries, assailing its “persistent refusal to address terrorism” emanating from Afghanistan’s soil.

It urged Kabul to recognise that the responsibility for addressing these threats “rests squarely with the Afghan Taliban regime”. “Pakistan’s resolve to protect its people must never be mistaken for weakness,” it declared.

Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), that are used for attacks in Pakistan.

stories.title: 1 dead, over 13 injured during stampede at TikToker's mehndi ceremony in Sialkot
summary: NAROWAL: A stampede at a mehndi (henna) event and prize-distribution ceremony held by a TikToker in Sialkot left one person dead and more than 13 others injured last night, police and rescue officials said on Saturday.

The mehndi ceremony and prize-distribution event for Muhammad Ansar Jatt, a popular TikToker from Sialkot district known as “Mr Pattlo”, was scheduled for Saturday night at Faraz Cricket Ground on Daska Road, according to a statement by Rescue 1122.

However, Sialkot residents Muhammad Asif and Aamir Ali stated that more than 40 people were injured in the stampede, explaining that before the rescue teams arrived, attendees had taken several injured to nearby private hospitals and clinics for first aid on their own.

stories.title: Fakhar Zaman and Arafat Minhas lead Pakistan to tri-series glory
summary: Pakistan chased down 326 to beat Sri Lanka by three wickets in the final of the tri-nation series on Saturday at a packed Gaddafi Stadium, sealing the title with nine balls to spare in what was the joint-highest successful chase in an ODI final.

Sri Lanka’s innings Pakistan had won the toss and elected to field, and the decision looked sound early as Sri Lanka’s openers Kamindu Mendis and Avishka Fernando scored briskly without risk, taking the visitors past 50 without loss inside ten overs.
From there on , Saad joined forces with Fakhar and steadied Pakistan’s innings.

stories.title: India opposition parties hold mock impeachment of poll chief
summary: India’s political opposition staged a symbolic impeachment of the election commissioner on Saturday to protest against a revision of voter lists that they say could unfairly benefit the ruling party.

The election commission says the initiative is necessary to ensure accurate voter lists, but the opposition claims it is being manipulated to favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Home Minister Amit Shah said the BJP was ready to hold a special session of parliament to discuss the revision. “But they (the opposition) have no intention of speaking there.

stories.title: ECP notifies delimitation schedule for Quetta, Kharian cantonment boards after reclassification
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has notified delimitation schedules for the Quetta and Kharian cantonment boards following their reclassification by the federal government.

The ECP has appointed the Gujrat district election commissioner as the convener of the delimitation committee for Kharian, with the Kharian cantonment executive officer and Gujrat assistant election commissioner as members.
The regional election commissioners for Gujranwala and Quetta have been appointed as delimitation authorities for the Kharian and Quetta cantonment boards, respectively, to decide objections.

stories.title: Sindh CM Murad blames city planners for 'ruining' Karachi
summary: Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah on Saturday blamed urban planners for “ruining” Karachi, adding that he saw the metropolis vastly expand and deteriorate firsthand while growing up in it.
Addressing an event of the Sindh Master Plan Authority (SMPA) in Karachi, CM Murad said: “Making a master plan from scratch is easy.
The chief minister said 14 master plans had been completed, but plans for Karachi and Hyderabad were under development.

stories.title: PHC seeks replies from governor, speaker against governor’s rule
summary: The petitions, filed in the Peshawar High Court by Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and others, contend that the imposition of emergency in certain districts and governor’s rule in others is unconstitutional and illegal.
The high court will take up the petitions for further hearing on November 10.
The petitioners were represented by lawyers Yasir Khattak and Azhar Rahim Khan, while K-P Advocate General Sanaullah and the relevant officials also appeared before the court.

stories.title: Mansehra assistant commissioner injured as vehicle comes under attack in Nowshera
summary: PESHAWAR: Mansehra Assistant Commissioner (AC) Adil Waseem was injured on Saturday when unknown gunmen opened fire at his official vehicle in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Nowshera district, officials said.
Waseem came under attack in Nowshera’s Panah Kot area while on his way back from his native village Saleh Khana in the district, police officials in Nowshera said.
According to Nowshera District Police Officer (DPO) Sonia Shamroz, the area was immediately cordoned off and a search operation was launched.

stories.title: Pakistan rebukes Afghan Taliban's 'deeply misguided approach' to resolving bilateral tensions
summary: Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Afghan Taliban administration to prevent terrorist organisations, particularly the TTP, from using its territory to launch attacks inside Pakistan.

Pakistan's position, according to officials, remains that Kabul must take concrete steps to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries, eliminate training infrastructure, prevent cross-border infiltration and ensure that Afghan territory is not used for attacks against Pakistan.

Pakistan says it expected the Taliban regime to fulfil its commitments by taking verifiable action against terrorist groups operating from its territory rather than defending or denying their presence.

stories.title: China green channel
summary: THE agreement between Islamabad and Beijing to set up a green channel at the Sost-Khunjerab border for agricultural and allied products should ease bilateral cross-border trade.
Last year, Pakistan Customs collected a record Rs15bn in revenue on imports through Khunjerab, while exports to China and Central Asia via the route came to just Rs2.8bn.
Beijing’s reported exports exceed Pakistan’s recorded imports from China by around $5bn, a gap that points to large-scale misdeclaration at the border and heavy revenue losses.

stories.title: Power bills and data centres cast rare spotlight on utilities in US midterms
summary: US electricity prices had flown under the radar in past national elections, but they have become a major political issue in this year’s midterms as Americans grow angry over rising utility bills and deals for power-hungry data centres.
Utilities spotlighted Seats on nine state public utility commissions are up for election this year, nearly all the US states where voters elect their utility regulators.

Power bills tracked low inflation for roughly a decade, and were not an issue in most mainstream elections until last year, when Mikie Sherrill successfully ran for New Jersey governor on the promise of freezing utility bills.

stories.title: Capt Safdar's remarks about women suffering from illness draw criticism, including from CM Maryam
summary: LAHORE: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz’s spouse, retired Capt Muhammad Safdar, has come under fire for disparaging remarks about women advocating for bodily autonomy.
Apart from CM Maryam, users on social media also took issue with Safdar’s remarks. “My [mother] has been a cancer patient, and God knows how we managed to get through those difficult times.

Lawyers’ bodies condemn remarks about Asma Jahangir Meanwhile, two premier lawyers’ bodies on Saturday strongly condemned Safdar for his remarks about Asma Jahangir – a renowned senior lawyer and human rights activist who passed away in 2018.

stories.title: Crypto exchanges call for quick moves to bolster defences after Binance heist
summary: Crypto exchanges are taking quick action to bolster their defences and urging greater industry-wide information-sharing after a record $6.3 billion hack of Binance exposed their vulnerability just as they become more embedded in mainstream finance.
Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, halted withdrawals after Thursday’s attack, which analysts blamed on North Korea and said it would use company funds to cover the losses.

Still, even as the industry reeled from the biggest cryptocurrency heist of all time, executives expressed confidence that Binance had sufficient resources to cover the losses and that the hack would not have broader financial repercussions.

stories.title: AI-based attendance system leads to dismissal of 72 doctors in Balochistan
summary: QUETTA: The Balochistan Health Department on Saturday dismissed 72 doctors from government service for prolonged absence from duty.

According to an official notification issued by the Balochistan health secretary, the action was taken under Section 4(B)(viii) of the Balochistan Employees’ Efficiency and Disciplinary Act (BEEDA), 2011.
In a statement, Balochistan Health Minister Bakht Muhammad Kakar said the doctors had repeatedly been issued notices directing them to report for duty, but they had failed to respond.

stories.title: Gen Z protests reach Germany as thousands join Halloween rallies
summary: Tens of thousands of people across Germany joined demonstrations on Saturday, as a youth-led movement inspired by protests elsewhere in Europe ‌took to the streets to demand better education and lower living costs.
The protests follow a wave of Gen Z-led demonstrations across Europe this year.
The German protests organised by the campaign group "Gen Z regelt" — "Gen Z takes charge" in German — ​are planned in 34 cities, including Berlin, Frankfurt and Munich.

stories.title: Iran's supreme leader warns US, Israel of 'unrestricted geographical response' to new attacks
summary: The remarks came during a reported meeting between Khamenei and senior military commanders, including armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, army chief Amir Hatami and Revolutionary Guards commander Ahmad Vahidi.
Khamenei has not been publicly seen since he became supreme leader, following his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei’s assassination in US-Israeli strikes at the start of the Middle East war in February.
It also said that Khamenei ordered the commanders to update Iran’s target list to include “all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist (Israeli) enemy”.

stories.title: Syria weighing whether to join Makkah pact: foreign minister
summary: Syria’s Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani on Saturday said Damascus was considering whether to join the Makkah defence pact that binds Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.
Pakistan is providing “whatever support is needed” to defend Saudi Arabia amid the Houthi attacks, the military’s spokesperson Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said earlier this month.
In August, two weeks after the Makkah pact was signed, the Syrian foreign minister visited Pakistan and called on Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir.

stories.title: Pakistan’s Punjab records 4.2 times more crop-fire detections than Indian Punjab: report
summary: LAHORE: Crop-fire detections in Pakistan’s Punjab were 4.2 times higher than in Indian Punjab during the first 29 days of October, according to satellite data, as the province grapples with worsening smog.

According to an analysis published by environmental monitoring website HamariHawa, Nasa satellites detected 13,241 fire spots in Pakistan’s Punjab between Oct 1 and 29, compared with 3,158 in Indian Punjab — 4.2 times as many detections.

A comparison based solely on data from the Suomi NPP satellite, which provides a consistent basis for examining trends over different years, showed that 4,562 fire spots were detected in Pakistan’s Punjab, compared with 918 in Indian Punjab, between Oct 1 and 29.

stories.title: Absence of department heads complicates PAC meetings
summary: Senior government officials are increasingly failing to attend meetings of the Punjab Assembly's Public Accounts Committee (PAC), sending junior officers in their place despite being summoned to respond to audit objections.

The absence of senior officials can delay the examination and settlement of audit objections, particularly when junior officers lack the authority to make decisions or provide final explanations on behalf of their departments.

Ensuring the participation of department secretaries and other responsible senior officials in PAC meetings remains important for strengthening parliamentary oversight, improving the resolution of audit objections and ensuring accountability for public expenditure.

stories.title: UK PM 'open' to slavery apology but not reparations
summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Saturday he was “open” to the UK issuing a formal apology for its role in the transatlantic slave trade, but ruled out financial reparations.
Britain’s central role in slavery and the treatment of people in its former colonies has loomed over the 77-year-old monarch’s Caribbean tour.
The UK has never formally apologised for slavery nor or agreed to pay reparations.

stories.title: Iranian strikes cause billions of dollars in damage to US bases: report
summary: The analysis found that, through August, more than 115 drone and missile strikes claimed by Iran or Iran-backed groups had damaged or destroyed structures at 26 military bases and other sites housing US equipment.

Read: 81 US aircraft lost or damaged during Iran war, congressional document shows The attacks have significantly altered the American military presence in the region, with the US moving many of its assets out of the Persian Gulf, two regional officials told the AP.

Early-warning systems among first targets Iran began its retaliation by striking systems designed to detect incoming attacks before expanding its targets to buildings and equipment that kept US bases operational, the report said.

stories.title: Trump says Russia-Ukraine deal could be near ahead of December’s G20 summit
summary: US President Donald Trump has expressed optimism about reaching a peace agreement between Russia and Ukraine, saying a deal could be close ahead of the December G20 summit at his Trump National Doral resort in Florida.
Asked about reports of a possible Russia-Ukraine agreement at the G20, Trump did not rule out the prospect, expressing confidence that negotiations could produce a breakthrough.
Trump claimed Iranian military capabilities had been severely weakened, adding that Washington would “finish that off”.

stories.title: Strange beaked 'hell chicken' is the first fruit-eating dinosaur
summary: This first-known frugivorous dinosaur, named Infernogallus jamesi, lived about ‌66 million years ago during the Cretaceous Period at the twilight of the age of dinosaurs and displayed traits on its beak and jaws for mashing soft food like fruit.
Infernogallus shows that some dinosaurs may have had a close ecological relationship with flowering plants.

"Mammals and birds would probably also have eaten fruit, but they didn't show the ⁠same kinds ​of specializations for a frugivorous diet that Infernogallus does, so it might have been a less important resource for ​them.

stories.title: Shooting at California Halloween store kills one, wounds six
summary: A shooting at a Halloween store in northern California killed one person and wounded six on Friday, police said, adding investigators had not yet identified who was responsible.
Fairfield Police Chief Dan Marshall told reporters one person was killed and six others were hospitalised with gunshot wounds.
The shooting took place near Florida Agricultural & Mechanical University’s campus on Perry Street, the university said, while police counted six adults and six juveniles among the injured.

stories.title: China's first shipborne stealth combat drone completes maiden carrier landing
summary: This represents yet another breakthrough made by China in the development of amphibious assault ships and marks that the Chinese Navy has acquired the capability to operate fixed-wing stealth drones from large maritime combat platforms, the navy source noted.
The Sichuan, hull number 51, is the first Type 076 amphibious assault ship designed and built independently by China.

Since beginning its first sea trials in November 2025, the Sichuan has steadily conducted various maritime tests as planned, successfully completing the debugging of various equipment and overall operational stability testing, the source said.

stories.title: Prime suspect in Gujranwala bride's murder killed in alleged exchange of fire, claims CCD
summary: LAHORE: The Crime Control Department (CCD) claimed on Saturday that the prime suspect in the murder of a bride on her wedding day in Gujranwala district was killed during an alleged exchange of fire.
According to a CCD spokesperson, the prime suspect, Sarfraz, had allegedly been hiding in Karachi with the other suspects before being arrested.
A day earlier, the CCD claimed that two alleged robbers were “killed during an encounter” in Punjab’s Kasur.

stories.title: Court grants bail to anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan, lawyer confirms
summary: KARACHI: A judicial magistrate granted bail to anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan, his lawyer, Advocate Ahmad Masood, confirmed to Dawn on Saturday.
On October 22, the same judicial magistrate rejected a bail plea filed by Hassan, prompting the defence to challenge the rejection in a sessions court.
On October 17, Hassan was produced before Judicial Magistrate Memon upon the completion of his initial four-day physical remand.

stories.title: Syria says discussions underway on joining Makkah Defence Alliance
summary: Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said on Saturday that "discussions are currently underway to evaluate Syria's entry into the Makkah alliance", a regional pact that brings together Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.
Shaibani’s remarks came during a regional security session at the Manama Dialogue 2026, according to the Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA).

Separately, the Syrian foreign minister said Israel has carried out more than 1,000 attacks on his country in less than two years, killing dozens of people. “Our territory has been subjected to more than 1,000 Israeli attacks in less than two years, killing dozens.

stories.title: Singapore FM’s visit focused on enhancing cooperation in trade, infrastructure and digital technologies: FO
summary: The two ministers also exchanged a memorandum of understanding on cooperation in disaster management between Pakistan’s National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) and Singapore’s Civil Defence Force (SCDF).

On Friday, Dr Balakrishnan met Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir at the General Headquarters, where the two discussed regional security and avenues for bilateral cooperation.
The two sides also exchanged views on regional and international developments and reaffirmed their commitment to continued engagement and cooperation at bilateral and multilateral fora.

stories.title: Police constable martyred, two injured in firing at Lakki Marwat judicial complex
summary: A police constable was martyred and two other people were injured when unidentified gunmen opened fire outside the courtroom of an additional sessions judge inside the Judicial Complex in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's (K-P's) Lakki Marwat on Saturday.
A day earlier, three policemen were martyred in separate incidents in K-P's Bannu, Lakki Marwat and Bajaur, while unidentified armed men abducted a head constable in Bannu.
In Lakki Marwat, unidentified armed men opened fire on Constable Mumtaz near a bank, martyring him.

stories.title: Rawalpindi police says legal action underway after man dies of 'police brutality' at Taxila check post
summary: The Rawalpindi police on Saturday initiated legal proceedings following the death of a 30-year-old man at the Gangu Police Check Post in Taxila, with a police spokesperson assuring that a fair investigation would be conducted and those responsible would be held accountable.
The incident reportedly occurred when a man, travelling from Khanpur towards Taxila, was stopped by police personnel at the Gangu checkpost for a search of his vehicle.

The same month, a resident accused personnel at RA Bazaar Police Station of torture, blackmail and extortion, while another case involved a 45-year-old man who sustained severe burn injuries after allegedly setting himself on fire at a police post.

stories.title: Three held for injuring scooty-riding female in Kasur
summary: KASUR: The A-Division police arrested three suspects on Friday for injuring a female college student by pushing her scooty at Baldia Chowk near the Government Girls College.

KABADDI: Sports inculcate discipline and a spirit of teamwork among youth and help them attain a healthy lifestyle, said Punjab Assembly Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmed Khan after a kabaddi match held at Khudian Khas in connection with Khelta Punjab on Friday.

He said the provincial government had initiated sports programmes to provide youth with a platform to showcase their talent and develop a healthy lifestyle instead of spending most of their time on mobile screens.

stories.title: Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab opens ‘Method and Madness’ exhibition
summary: https://www.dawn.com/news/2041073

stories.title: Three-year-old child tests positive for mpox in Sindh
summary: KARACHI: Another child tested positive for mpox in the city on Friday, raising the tally of the viral infectious disease this year so far in the province to 115.
With the latest case, the total number of mpox cases reported this year so far at SIDH&RC has risen to 31, while in the province to 115 with 12 deaths.
The team sealed the facility following reports that a child seemed to have contracted mpox there.

stories.title: UK PM Burnham says he is 'open' to formal apology for slavery, but rules out reparations
summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was open to calls for a formal apology for Britain's historical role in slavery, ​before attending next week's Commonwealth summit at which he is likely ‌to face demands for financial reparations.

Writing in the Guardian newspaper, Burnham said Britain was "offering a structured dialogue with those affected by the transatlantic slave trade", in which at ​least 12.5 million Africans were abducted and sold into slavery.

Ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda next week, King Charles, who is touring the Caribbean, said it was "only right that we should ​acknowledge the great suffering ​and injustices of ⁠the past".

stories.title: PM criticises PTI's 13-year rule in K-P, urges PML-N leadership to prioritise public welfare projects
summary: While criticising PTI, the prime minister said political slogans and divisive politics had taken precedence over public service, while problems in Peshawar, Kohistan, Hazara and the southern districts remained unaddressed.
PM Shehbaz was wary that the federal government had repeatedly called for collective efforts against terrorism, but its appeals had not received the desired response from the PTI-led government.
The premier said a decision had become necessary to protect the people, the country, the economy and society, adding that any delay could have caused further damage to the province.

stories.title: Trump admin approves potential Patriot missiles sale to Ukraine
summary: The Trump administration on Friday green-lit the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine, the State Department said, but the Ukrainian president warned deliveries could take years.
The statement did not provide an estimate for when the weapons could be delivered to Ukraine.
The State Department said the weapons sale would be paid for with by donations from Ukraine’s allies but not with US funds.

stories.title: Trump administration plans to deport Afghan refugees to Pakistan: report
summary: The Trump administration is preparing to deport Afghan refugees to Pakistan as early as Monday, despite concerns that they could subsequently be returned to Afghanistan under Taliban rule, media reports said Friday.
AfghanEvac, an organisation advocating for Afghan refugees, criticised the administration’s reported deportation plans in a statement Friday.
The reported flight would come after months of uncertainty over the future of Afghan refugees at the Qatar facility, as the administration continues considering arrangements for their removal.
